summary.headline: RBL Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 170% YoY to INR482 crore, with advances up 42% YoY to INR1,42,314 crore on FCNR-led liquidity.
summary.overview: RBL Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of INR482 crore, up 170% YoY and 90% QoQ, with NII up 37% YoY to INR2,131 crore and NIM at 4.61%, up 48 bps QoQ. Growth was driven by FCNR(B) mobilisation and the capital raise, which together added about 35% to the balance sheet, now at INR2,22,344 crore. Asset quality improved, with GNPA down 28 bps QoQ to 1.02% and specific credit cost down to 52 bps from 62 bps, while cards slippages are guided lower. Management guided NIM slightly lower in Q3 and up in Q4, and declined to give FY28 ROA or margin targets; the bank expects Q3 and Q4 opex growth of 7-8% and the ENBD India amalgamation to complete in FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR771 crore (63 bps); specific credit cost INR641 crore (52 bps)
financial_highlights.change: Specific cost was INR670 crore (62 bps) in Q1
GNPA -28 bps QoQ; Net NPA -8 bps QoQ
+34% YoY; ex-FCNR +6% YoY; average deposits +24% YoY

financial_highlights.value: INR42,526 crore; average CASA ratio 24% (28.1% ex-FCNR)

financial_highlights.change: +12% YoY, +13% QoQ (includes one-off FCNR-related swap fee)

segments.name: Wholesale
segments.commentary: Advances grew 56% YoY; corporate book +60% YoY and commercial banking +47% YoY. Growth is mainly working-capital driven, with some project finance, and the sector mix shows no single standout.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 32% YoY; secured retail +52% YoY (includes about INR10,300 crore FCNR leverage to customers) and unsecured retail +11% YoY. Retail:wholesale mix is 56:44. Cards are guided to low-to-high single-digit to low-double-digit growth.

segments.name: Cards
segments.commentary: Cards provisioning was about INR575 crore in the quarter on a book of about INR19,000-20,000 crore. September monthly slippages were INR125-130 crore, and card slippages are expected around INR400 crore per quarter in Q3-Q4, taking card credit cost from low double digits toward about 6%.

segments.name: Microfinance
segments.commentary: Year-on-year growth is strong at about 25%, but sequential growth is guided at 5-6%. Management says the book is held for PSL purposes rather than as a growth engine.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Banca income is about INR300 crore per annum. Management expects a 50-60% impact if the draft IRDAI circular is implemented as drafted.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 NIM expected slightly lower than Q2, with an inch-up in Q4 as the repo hike flows through.
Opex growth guided at about 7-8%; management said it could move to low single digits, possibly a little higher, as branch, people and wealth investments build.
Card credit cost expected to fall from about 11% toward 5.5-6%, with card slippages around INR400 crore in Q3 and Q4.

Advances baseline growth of 22-25% YoY is the stated minimum, implying about 5-6% QoQ; FY27 unsecured growth is guided at high single digits to low double digits, and loan growth at 15-20% for next year.

ENBD India amalgamation is pending RBI approval and is expected to complete in this financial year. Branch expansion targets about 30-50 branches per quarter, with 1,000 branches in about 2.5-3 years.
capex_capacity: About 38 new branches were due to open in the weeks after the call, in line with a 30-50 branches per quarter pace.
Normal LCR is 120-125% over time; current LCR of 148% leaves room to deploy excess liquidity.

Liquidity from capital raise and FCNR(B) is about 35% of the balance sheet as of 31 May 2026; management expects this to be deployed over the next few months in short-term investments and wholesale loans.
AFS book is INR43,000 crore versus INR37,700 crore in the prior quarter; management kept duration light.
Retail term deposits grew about 16% in the quarter, after 20-22% in each of the prior two quarters.
demand_pricing: Advances yield fell from 11.2% to 10.8%; management attributes this to mix (wholesale up, unsecured down) and FCNR leverage, and says excluding FCNR leverage the yield would be 10-15 bps higher.
Cost of time deposits is 6.86% (FCNR plus INR), and INR TD is 7.12%; CASA cost is about 5.97%, and total cost of funds is falling QoQ.
Ex-FCNR deposit growth is 6% YoY; management is prioritising lower-cost deposits and let high-cost bulk term deposits run down.
Loan book is about 58% linked to external benchmarks, with 32% to repo (90-day reset) and about 11% to FBIL.
Corporate deposit rates have fallen on rating upgrades, and the bank is adding customers in wholesale for both advances and deposits.

qa_highlights.question: Why did period-end CASA rise about 15% QoQ while average CASA was flat, and what is being done to build the retail franchise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the flat average reflects deliberate exits of high-cost CASA after rate cuts, and it expects recovery within 4-5 months. Branch densification and expansion, plus affluent and wealth segments with ENBD support, are the levers. Retail term deposits grew about 16%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory for Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep Iyer guided Q3 blended NIM slightly lower than Q2 because liquidity sits in lower-yielding investments, with a probable inch-up in Q4 from the repo hike flow-through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the bancassurance draft circular?
qa_highlights.answer: Banca income is about INR300 crore per year, and management expects a 50-60% impact on it if the draft circular is implemented as written.

qa_highlights.question: What is the card slippage and credit cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: September monthly card slippages were INR125-130 crore, card slippages are expected around INR400 crore per quarter in Q3-Q4, and card credit cost should move from about 11% to about 6%. Cards provisioning in Q2 was about INR575 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY28 ROA and growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give an FY28 ROA target and said it will come back in a few months. It pointed to the current 0.92% RoA and said FCNR and equity liquidity are a fixed-rate tailwind to margins and growth.

qa_highlights.question: How will advances growth be sustained, and what is the SA growth expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a 22-25% baseline (about 5-6% QoQ) and did not link loan growth to a single CASA metric; it expects SA growth from branch expansion, NRI and trade corridor business.

risks_watch: Margin compression as liquidity is deployed at lower yields, with cost of funds only partly falling and the deposit mix still weak (CASA 24% average).
Bancassurance fee income could fall 50-60% (about INR300 crore per year) if the IRDAI draft circular is implemented as written.
Card credit cost depends on slippages falling from INR125-130 crore a month to about INR400 crore a quarter; any reversal would hit credit cost.
Rising repo rate (6.5%) and possible further hikes, with monsoon and Middle East risks to rural and retail collections.
Pending RBI approval for ENBD India amalgamation; timing and terms for the FY27 completion remain open.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and growth momentum, but cautious and evasive on forward margin, FY28 ROA and deposit-cost guidance, repeatedly citing too many moving parts. Management was also defensive on the reconciliation of FCNR-driven balance sheet growth and running down of time deposits.
key_quotes: Our advances grew this quarter by 42% year-on-year to INR1,42,314 crores and average advances grew 33% year-on-year.
Now let us settle down with the current 0.92 RoA and how it is looking positive for the next couple of quarters.

adds.what: About 38 new branches opening in weeks after call; pace of 30-50 branches per quarter, targeting 1,000 branches in about 2.5-3 years
ENBD India amalgamation (inorganic, pending RBI approval) - not own capacity build

growth.why: Management guides advances growth of at least 22-25% YoY (baseline held) and loan growth of 15-20% next year, with opex growth of 7-8% and card credit cost falling toward 6%; delivery rests on working-capital and corporate wholesale demand, liquidity deployment and branch rollout, but no specific orders or contracts with numbers were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q3 NIM guided slightly lower than Q2's 4.61%, with only a probable inch-up in Q4 from repo hike flow-through; advances yield fell 11.2% to 10.8% and FY28 margin target was declined.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 38 branches opening in weeks after the call, in line with a 30-50 per quarter pace toward 1,000 branches in about 2.5-3 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 42% YoY to INR1,42,314 crore, with a stated minimum of 22-25% YoY (about 5-6% QoQ) and loan growth of 15-20% guided for next year.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give FY28 ROA or margin targets and is cautious on forward margin and deposit-cost guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Opex guided at 7-8% (could move to low single digits or a little higher), NIM guided lower in Q3, and bancassurance income (about INR300 crore a year) could fall 50-60% if the IRDAI draft circular is implemented.

rows.label: Card credit cost normalising to about 6%
rows.why: Card slippages guided to about INR400 crore per quarter in Q3-Q4 (September monthly slippages INR125-130 crore), down from card provisioning of about INR575 crore in Q2, with card credit cost falling from about 11% to 5.5-6%.

rows.label: ENBD India amalgamation
rows.why: Approved by the bank's side and pending RBI approval, with completion guided within this financial year; no capacity or numbers given.

rows.label: Deployment of excess liquidity
rows.why: Capital raise and FCNR(B) liquidity is about 35% of the balance sheet and LCR is 148% against a normal 120-125%, so management expects deployment into short-term investments and wholesale loans.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality, card credit normalisation and advances momentum, but cautious and evasive on forward NIM, FY28 ROA, and deposit-cost guidance; analysts pressed on margin trajectory, FCNR-driven balance sheet growth and time deposit run-down.

oneOffs.what: One-off FCNR-related swap fee included in fee income of INR1,040 crore (+12% YoY, +13% QoQ); size not quantified in the brief
